title: Add tool-calling example + golden fixtures (handle partial args during streaming)
author: Mateusz Zielinski
release_notes:
- Go SDK: add runnable tool-calling example with streaming-safe argument assembly
- Tests: add golden fixtures for streaming tool-call event sequences (incl. partial args)
description:
Context: As part of the streaming/tool-calling examples refresh, we need a runnable Go example that matches the canonical event model and a small set of fixtures to keep behavior stable across releases. We’ve also had customer confusion around tool-call args looking “truncated” mid-stream (SUP-18421). This PR adds an example + tests that explicitly demonstrate how to assemble tool-call arguments across deltas.

What’s included: 1) New example: cmd/examples/tool_calling_streaming/main.go (and README) demonstrating: - Defining tools with JSON schema-ish parameters (kept small and copy/paste friendly) - Streaming loop that handles: message deltas, tool_call deltas, and final assembly - Correct handling of partial tool-call arguments: accumulate string fragments until the final tool_call message is complete before json.Unmarshal - Executing multiple tool calls sequentially (example shows 2 calls) and sending tool results back as tool-result messages

2) Golden fixtures + tests: - Added fixtures under internal/testdata/golden/tool_calls/*.jsonl capturing a few “representative” transcripts: a) tool-call args split across multiple events b) tool-call args split at UTF-8 boundary (defensive) c) parallel-ish tool calls emitted back-to-back (model emits multiple tool_call entries before final)
- Added TestStreamingToolCallsGolden that replays event JSONL into the assembler and asserts stable output (final assistant message + tool call list).

Notes / caveats documented in the example: - During streaming, tool_call.arguments may be partial; do not parse until you see the final tool_call completion event / finish_reason. - Do not assume each chunk is valid JSON. Treat args as an opaque string buffer until complete. - Fixtures strip request_id/timestamps to avoid flake.

Why fixtures in Go repo: we want a language-local guardrail so the example doesn’t drift when we touch the stream consumer loop (ENG-4825). This is meant to be small/fast (runs in <1s) and does not hit the network.

Checklist: - [x] Example is runnable end-to-end with REDWOOD_API_KEY - [x] Example output is deterministic given fixtures - [x] Tests added + run in CI - [x] Comments call out partial args pitfall + reference SUP-18421

Follow-ups: We may later expand to show true parallel tool execution (goroutines) once we finalize the recommended pattern; for now the example keeps execution serial to be easiest to copy/paste.
commits: examples(go): add streaming tool calling example with args assembler
tests(go): add golden transcript fixtures for tool calling stream
tests(go): add replay harness + assertions for final message/tool calls
docs(go): clarify partial tool args during streaming in example README
chore: normalize fixture fields (strip timestamps/request ids)
checks: CI / fixtures lint (strip volatile fields): pass
conversation:
Ibrahim Khan (review): This is the right direction. Two nits: (1) please make it explicit in the example that args buffers can be invalid JSON mid-stream; (2) the golden fixtures should not include request_id-like fields or timestamps. Also, can we add a small comment referencing the support ticket about “truncated args” so folks understand why we buffer?

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Good call. Updated README + inline comments to say args are opaque until completion; added a section “Why args look truncated” and referenced SUP-18421. Also added a fixture normalizer that strips request_id/created_at-ish fields before committing the JSONL.

Brian Murphy (review): The assembler currently attempts json.Unmarshal on every delta if the buffer ends with '}'. That’s not safe (nested braces, strings, etc.). We should only parse once we know the tool_call is complete (finish_reason or explicit final event).

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Agreed. Removed the 'endsWith' heuristic. Now we parse only when we receive a completed tool_call entry (event indicates tool_call is finalized). Added a test case where args buffer contains braces inside a string.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI note: golden tests are great but can flake if ordering differs. Please ensure deterministic ordering for tool calls in the assembled output, or assert as a set with stable sort.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Sorted tool calls by (tool_call_id, index) in the assembler output before asserting. Updated tests accordingly.

Sabrina James (review): Example reads well. Minor: rename variables from tc to toolCall for readability; and please ensure the tool result message uses the exact role/name field expected in other language examples.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Renamed variables, and aligned the tool-result message shape to match the parity guidelines (role=tool, tool_call_id set, content is the tool output).
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Looks solid now. The README callout on partial args + the fixtures make this much safer for copy/paste. Approved.
Brian Murphy (approval): Thanks for removing the heuristic parsing. Approved.
Sahana Iyer (approval): CI is clean; fixture linter is a nice touch. Approved.
